seats.name: seat-1
argv:
Read spec.txt (the STAMP language) and program.stamp. Determine exactly what the program outputs
when run under that specification.

Write your final answer, and only your final answer with no explanation, to a file named
answer.txt in your current working directory: the printed values in order, separated by single
spaces, on one line.

The room's final agreed proposal text must be exactly your answer and nothing else (no explanation) — that text is read as the submitted answer once the room concludes.

Join room rq1 as seat-1 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
Done. All three participants independently derived the same output and reached unanimous consensus. `answer.txt` contains:

```
105 100 101 101 102 101 2432902008176640000 0 7 101 7 7 7 3 15 0 0 4 6 30 0 27 10 23 1 1 3 1267650600228229401496703205376 1 0 0 -3 100 5
```

The trickiest part was confirming `DEF outer`/`DEF inner` has no lexical closures — `inner`'s reference to `a` falls back to the global (`0`), not outer's local parameter — which all three independent interpreters (mine included) confirmed, giving `100` and `5` for the final two prints.

seats.name: seat-2
argv:
Read spec.txt (the STAMP language) and program.stamp. Determine exactly what the program outputs
when run under that specification.

Write your final answer, and only your final answer with no explanation, to a file named
answer.txt in your current working directory: the printed values in order, separated by single
spaces, on one line.

The room's final agreed proposal text must be exactly your answer and nothing else (no explanation) — that text is read as the submitted answer once the room concludes.

Join room rq1 as seat-2 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
The room concluded unanimously (3/3) on the answer, which matches what's already written to `answer.txt`:

```
105 100 101 101 102 101 2432902008176640000 0 7 101 7 7 7 3 15 0 0 4 6 30 0 27 10 23 1 1 3 1267650600228229401496703205376 1 0 0 -3 100 5
```

The trickiest part (flagged by two challenges, both resolved) was the nested `DEF inner` inside `DEF outer`: STAMP has no lexical closures, so `inner`'s read of `a` falls back to the global (never set → 0) rather than outer's call-local `a=1`, giving `CALL outer 1 = 100` and `CALL inner 5 = 5`. Three independently-written interpreters (mine plus seat-1's and seat-3's) agreed on the full output.

seats.text:
Task complete. The room concluded unanimously on:

```
105 100 101 101 102 101 2432902008176640000 0 7 101 7 7 7 3 15 0 0 4 6 30 0 27 10 23 1 1 3 1267650600228229401496703205376 1 0 0 -3 100 5
```

This is already written to `answer.txt` in the workspace. The trickiest part was the nested `DEF inner` inside `DEF outer` — the spec has no lexical closures (only local-to-call vs. global), so `inner`'s reference to `a` falls back to global `a=0`, not outer's local `a=1`. All three seats independently wrote interpreters and converged on the same output, including that edge case.
